events.title: The Battle of Hastings
events.shortBlurb: On Senlac Hill near Hastings, King Harold fell with his brothers, and William of Normandy's victory began the remaking of England and her Church…
body: Harold had been king nine months. On 25 September 1066 he destroyed the invading Norsemen at Stamford Bridge; three days later William of Normandy landed at Pevensey, carrying — the Norman writers say — a banner blessed by Pope Alexander II. Forced marches brought Harold south to meet him with a weary army.

The battle was fought on 14 October 1066 on the hill of Senlac, seven miles from Hastings, and lasted from morning to dusk. The old account remarks the temper of the two camps the night before: the Normans prayed and prepared for Communion while the English caroused. By nightfall Harold and his brothers Gyrth and Leofwine lay dead, and with them the flower of the English thegnhood.

William was crowned in Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day. The Conquest remade the English Church as well as the realm: Stigand was deposed and Lanfranc of Bec came to Canterbury, councils reformed the clergy, and new cathedrals rose in the Norman manner. On the battlefield itself William raised Battle Abbey, its high altar over the spot where Harold fell.
